T0604.title: Residential Proxy
T0604.definition: A proxy resource sourced from IPs assigned by real home-broadband ISPs, belonging to real carriers and geographies, with high reputation that makes it the hardest for proxy detection to block — the first choice for black-market scraping and credential stuffing to evade IP risk control.
T0604.description: Proxy IP resources are mainly classified into three types by source and form: residential proxies, datacenter proxies, and tunneling proxies. Residential proxies originate from IPs assigned by real home-broadband ISPs, belong to real carriers and geographies, carry high reputation and are the hardest for proxy detection (A0038) to block, making them the first choice for black-market scraping and credential stuffing — and the most expensive. By contrast, datacenter proxies originate from cloud datacenters and IDCs — cheap, highly concurrent, and low-latency, but their IP ranges clearly belong to datacenters, making them easy for IP intelligence (A0016-001) and proxy detection to flag. Tunneling proxies achieve single-ingress dynamic forwarding to a large number of egress IPs, enabling single-access-point IP rotation. Because residential proxies belong to real ISPs and are hard to distinguish from normal user traffic, they are the hardest type to identify in anti-scraping defense. They are commonly integrated into a proxy pool (AT0098) for on-demand scheduling, and together with IP providers (TA0011) form the black-market IP supply chain, used to evade IP rate limiting, blocklists, and geo-fencing.
T0604.usageExample: A scraping gang rents a residential proxy pool to evade IP rate limiting, keeping each egress IP's request frequency below the threshold to bypass cloud anti-scraping.
